To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the next-to-next-leading order (NNLO) corrections are substantial for the ADD and RS models of TeV scale gravity, and that they are larger than the next-to-leading-order corrections.
the NLO corrections to graviton production in the ADD and RS models are large, of the order of 50%, and the NNLO corrections are also large and positive, increasing the cross section by another 10%.
the NNLO corrections to the Drell- Yan cross section are large and positive, and that the NNLO K factors for the total cross section in the RS model are between 1.10 and 1.13.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the next-to-next-leading order QCD correction to the production of the Kaluza-Klein gravitons at the LHC within the framework of the ADD model and the RS model.
the calculation of the two-loop QCD corrections to processes involving gravitons, and with the evaluation of the theoretical uncertainty associated to the computation.
the computation of next-to-next-to leading order corrections to the production of a single graviton in models of extra dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NLO corrections are large and positive, and the NNLO corrections are large, negative and of opposite sign.
the NNLO QCD corrections increase the cross section by 10%–20%, depending on the model and on the kinematical cuts.
these results are important for the LHC phenomenology of TeV-scale models of quantum gravity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NNLO QCD corrections to graviton production in TeV-scale gravity models is large, and should be considered in the experimental searches for these particles.

the inclusion of the NNLO QCD corrections in the ADD model is essential in order to extract reliable predictions from the data, and the NNLO corrections to the RS model are important for the region of graviton masses below 2 TeV.
the NNLO QCD corrections are large and reduce substantially the uncertainty of the theoretical predictions in both models of TeV gravity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inclusion of the NNLO corrections is necessary in order to obtain accurate predictions for the production of TeV-scale gravitons in the Drell-Yann and in the single graviton channels at hadron colliders, and to reduce the theoretical uncertainties.
the NNLO soft-virtual corrections are large and reduce the scale uncertainty in the theoretical prediction.
, in the region where gravitons are produced in the TeV range, the NNLO corrections can be substantial and should be taken into account.
